module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1090

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1090](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1090)
- [Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1090

/--
Let $k\geq 3$. Does there exist a finite set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ such that, in any $2$-colouring of $A$, there exists a line which contains at least $k$ points from $A$, and all the points of $A$ on the line have the same colour?

Erdős [Er75f] says Graham and Selfridge proved the answer is yes when $k=3$. Hunter has observed that, for sufficiently large $n$, a generic projection of $[k]^n$ into $\mathbb{R}^2$ has this property, by the Hales-Jewett theorem.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1090.lean"]
theorem erdos_1090 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ), ∀ (hk : 3 ≤ k),
    ∃ (A : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)), ∀ (C : A → Fin 2),
      ∃ (S : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)), ∃ (hSA : S ⊆ A),
        Collinear ℝ (S : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) ∧ S.card ≥ k ∧
          (∀ y ∈ A, y ∈ affineSpan ℝ (S : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) → y ∈ S) ∧
          ∃ c, ∀ x (hx : x ∈ S), C ⟨x, hSA hx⟩ = c := by
  sorry

end Erdos1090

reformulations.difference: The source quantifies over lines L in the plane: "a line which contains at least k points from A, and all the points of A on the line have the same colour". The Lean never quantifies over lines. It asks for a Finset S ⊆ A with `Collinear ℝ S`, `S.card ≥ k`, the closure condition `∀ y ∈ A, y ∈ affineSpan ℝ S → y ∈ S` (so that S = A ∩ affineSpan S), and S monochromatic. The line is implicit as `affineSpan ℝ S`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Source ⇒ Lean: take S = A ∩ L. S lies in a line, so it is collinear, and |S| ≥ k. Since affineSpan S ≤ L, every y ∈ A in affineSpan S lies in S. S is monochromatic by assumption. Lean ⇒ Source: |S| ≥ k ≥ 3 gives two distinct points p ≠ q in S. Collinearity gives `line[ℝ,p,q] = affineSpan ℝ S` (Mathlib `Collinear.affineSpan_eq_of_ne`). The closure condition then gives A ∩ line[ℝ,p,q] = S, which has at least k points, all of one colour. The k ≥ 3 hypothesis rules out a degenerate S whose affine span is not a line. In /workspace/review/equiv.lean I proved `type_of% @Erdos1090.erdos_1090 ↔ (True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 3, ∃ A : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ), ∀ C : A → Fin 2, ∃ p q, p ≠ q ∧ k ≤ #(A.filter (· ∈ line[ℝ,p,q])) ∧ ∃ c, ∀ x (hx : x ∈ A), x ∈ line[ℝ,p,q] → C ⟨x,hx⟩ = c)`. `#print axioms` shows only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Using `Fin 2 → ℝ` (sup-norm) instead of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` does not matter, because only affine notions appear.

review.notes:
No defects found. The single declaration faithfully states the question as posed by erdosproblems.com, which follows [Er75f]: "Does there exist for every k a set of points in the plane so that if one colors the points by two colors in an arbitrary way, there always should be at least one line which contains at least k points and all whose points have the same color. GRAHAM and SELFRIDGE gave an affirmative answer for k = 3". In context this is about property B for lines determined by a point set, so "all whose points" means all points of the set on the line. The Lean closure condition captures exactly this; an earlier AI-generated formal statement mentioned on the forum missed it.

Erdős's original wording does not say "finite", while erdosproblems.com and the Lean do. Since the answer is affirmative, the finite version is the stronger positive claim and implies the unrestricted one. This is not an issue.

The docstring, `answer(True)`, `research solved` and the `formal_proof` record all agree with the source ("PROVED (LEAN) … solved in the affirmative").

On the formal_proof link: the linked file targets Lean/Mathlib v4.29.1 and does not compile verbatim under this repo's v4.33.1. There are four tactic-drift errors in auxiliary lemmas, plus one in the weaker theorem `exists_set_with_monochromatic_line_property`, which the strict theorem does not use. I patched only the proofs of those auxiliary lemmas, in a scratch copy, with no statement changes. With that, `theorem fc_erdos_1090_holds : type_of% @Erdos1090.erdos_1090` is proved from `Erdos1090.exists_set_with_strict_monochromatic_line_property`, depending only on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The linked theorem's statement is verbatim the FC right-hand side, so the formal_proof claim is valid. The link uses the repo-wide `blob/main/src/v4.29.1/...` convention (290 files).

Boundary checks: k ≥ 3 guarantees |S| ≥ 3, so affineSpan S is a genuine line. Singletons and the empty set cannot qualify. Constant colourings are included, which is the standard reading of "any 2-colouring". The statement is not trivially true: it needs the Hales–Jewett/generic-projection construction.
